r3CounterexampleReproduction.observed: A coherent request and upstream mutation of casHead and idempotencyKey against unchanged signed authoritative snapshots returned DENY with AUTHORITATIVE_CAS_HEAD_MISMATCH and an all-zero effect ledger. Same-key/same-bytes replay returned REPLAY_NOOP; different bytes and atomic loser denied with zero effects.

A cost record after authorization expiry returned COST_OUTSIDE_AUTHORIZATION_WINDOW; proof before the sealed record returned COST_PROVIDER_PROOF_TIME_INVALID; a minimally typed unsigned reference stub returned COST_RESERVATION_REFERENCE_INVALID; checkedNanoSum rejected Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER plus one with NANOUSD_OVERFLOW.
A resealed summary with raw A01 observed=fail and summary A01/pass returned TT_RAW_SUMMARY_MISMATCH. A provider-proof signature tamper returned TT_PROVIDER_PROOF_SIGNATURE_INVALID.
A resealed RC-LEGAL-SIGNED-LOG event with boundaryAt forged to terminalAt plus 60 seconds returned LIFECYCLE_DERIVED_BOUNDARY_MISMATCH with an all-zero effect ledger.

Empty or mutually equal unrelated pre/post inventories returned RECOVERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH. Adding a source before its cut or deleting a required cut source returned RECOVERY_CUT_SOURCE_UNREACHABLE, all with zero effects.
The candidate remains deliberately unsigned and non-canonical. This review did not require prior canonicalization and makes no finding merely from that state.

decision.rationale: All 44 manifest entries match and the five R3 technical counterexamples now fail closed, but independent execution found a protected-action authorization bypass: the shared decision function ignores the manifest's exactPath and allowedPathClasses controls and does not require requiredUpstreamAction to name an enumerated authorized action. A coherently signed github.exam.candidate.commit targeting the Gate 2 signature path returned ALLOW, and migration.expand/backfill return ALLOW with migration.plan.authorize even though that upstream action is absent from the exhaustive manifest. The bundled validator also continues to leave declared negative matrices and sanitized-real controls as unexecuted labels. Zero blocker/major is not met, so the candidate is not technically ready for authorized incorporation.

originalFindingDispositions.basis: R4-PF-001 demonstrates that the Exam-author commit action can target intent/0001/signatures/gate-2.json because exactPath is not enforced.

The policy text and class-bound lifecycle path are substantially strengthened, but the declared sanitized-real provenance, identifier, linkage, inspection, use-authorization, derivative, and raw-receipt cases remain label-only and are not executed by the candidate validator.

The signed Trusted Tester record now binds exact environments, A01-A81 raw lines, summary derivation, qualification/assignment times, revisions, and cryptographically verified provider proof; contradiction and tamper counterexamples deny.

The spend schema and record semantics are materially improved, but the protected commit path that carries a spend authorization does not enforce its declared exact path class, leaving the authorization-oracle chain incomplete under R4-PF-001.

The record schemas and direct R3 temporal/reference checks are corrected, but the normative cost vector suite and several declared negative classes are not consumed or exhaustively executed by validate-remediation.mjs under R4-PF-002.
The candidate uses checked nonnegative integer nanoUSD and BigInt aggregation with explicit overflow rejection; the required R3 overflow counterexample fails.

The fixed 16-class table, signed trigger history, class-specific durations, derived inventories, parent caps, and forged-boundary rejection make the technical policy contract determinate. The qualified human policy ruling remains a dependency.

The corrected recovery decision derives canonical and restored inventories, binds record cursors and exact bytes, rejects unavailable cut state and unrelated inventories, and preserves provider acknowledgement as authority. Live provider capability and rehearsal remain release dependencies.

R4-PF-001 shows migration.expand and migration.backfill accept migration.plan.authorize although that action is absent from the manifest's exhaustive action set; the irreversible authorization chain is not closed.

Non-circular revisions and explicit JCS omission preimages, SHA-256 digests, Ed25519 signatures, and duplicate-key rejection are executable.

The corrected recovery logic closes R3-PF-005, but the validator does not execute the declared nineteen recovery corruption/retry cases, so every-cut adversarial completeness remains unproved.

newFindings.title: Protected-action decision ignores manifest path and upstream-action authorization
counterexamples: Starting from github.exam.candidate.commit, R4 changed request.body.selectors.path to intent/0001/signatures/gate-2.json, recomputed immutableRequestDigest, resealed the upstream envelope with identical selectors, resealed the signed current CAS snapshot for that path, and resealed the atomic reservation for the new request digest. The request schema returned no errors and protectedActionDecision returned ALLOW with credentialAccess=1, installationToken=1, and providerRequest=1, despite the manifest's exactPath being intent/0001/EXAM.md.

The exhaustive manifest contains no migration.plan.authorize action. Nevertheless, AUTH_PROFILES requires that upstream action for migration.expand and migration.backfill, makeAuthorizationFixture creates it, and protectedActionDecision returns ALLOW because it compares only the hard-coded profile string and never requires the upstream action to exist in the manifest.
newFindings.impact: A validly signed and current caller-controlled envelope can move a protected Exam-author operation onto a signature or other path and can invoke migration from an authorization action that policy declares nonexistent. Exact-path separation, exhaustive deny-by-default policy, and independently authorized migration are therefore bypassed before provider effects.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Make the decision function enforce exactPath and every allowedPathClasses expression from the selected manifest action against the immutable request; deny zero or multiple path-class matches. Select requiredUpstreamAction and requiredActorRole from the manifest rather than a parallel hard-coded profile, require the upstream action to exist in the same exhaustive manifest, and validate its principal, role, credential, decision/assignment record and delegation chain. Add coherent wrong-path cases for Exam, decision, spend, lifecycle tombstone, and normal item commits, plus missing/unlisted/wrong-role migration-plan and cleanup authorization cases, all with zero effects.

newFindings.title: Declared adversarial matrices and sanitized-real controls are still not executed
newFindings.impact: The package can print PASS without consuming the structured authorizationCases, lifecycleCases, recoveryCases, spendRecordCases, sanitizedRealCases, or normative COST-ORACLE-VECTORS rows. It also does not execute the declared authorizationByteMutations, lifecycle boundary-by-precedence and raw-grant matrices, lifecycle special cases, or nineteen recovery corruptions. The green result therefore does not prove the package's claimed exhaustive negative, race, privacy, cost, lifecycle, or recovery contract.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Drive every normative fixture and vector through the applicable schema and shared semantic decision function, compare the exact expected state and first error, assert typed zero effects for every denial/failure, and fail validation if any declared case ID or coverage kind is unexecuted. Implement executable sanitized-real provenance, identifier, named-entity, four-token uniqueness, k-anonymity, linkage/Wilson, use-authorization, independent-inspection, derivative, raw-receipt, and destination-segregation inputs rather than label rows.
